The vibration damping device (10) is constructed around a central axis (O) and comprises a tubular outer attachment member (11) and an inner attachment member (12), which are positioned in a coaxial arrangement. These two attachment members are connected to one another through a pair of main rubber portions (13), which are strategically spaced apart along the central axis (O). ## Partition Portion and Liquid Chamber Division

Between the two main rubber portions (13), a liquid chamber (25) is formed. To regulate the fluid dynamics within this chamber, a partition portion (15) is incorporated into the design. This partition portion (15) serves a dual function: it couples the outer attachment member (11) and the inner attachment member (12) together, while simultaneously dividing the liquid chamber (25) into two distinct sections—a first liquid chamber (26) and a second liquid chamber (27). This division is essential for enabling controlled fluid movement between the two chambers, which contributes to the damping performance of the device.

## Structural Composition of the Partition Portion

The partition portion (15) itself is composed of two primary structural elements:

1. **Annular Rigid Portion (30):** This component contains a restricted passage (33), which serves as a fluid pathway connecting the first liquid chamber (26) and the second liquid chamber (27). The restricted nature of this passage allows fluid to flow between the chambers in a controlled manner, generating the damping effect necessary for vibration attenuation.

2. **Annular Elastic Portion (29):** Positioned adjacent to the annular rigid portion (30) in the radial direction, this elastic component works in conjunction with the rigid portion to provide additional flexibility and responsiveness to the partition assembly.

## Functional Interaction Between Elastic and Rigid Portions

A key design feature of this vibration damping device lies in the relationship between the elastic portion (29) and the rigid portion (30). The elastic portion (29) is specifically engineered to undergo compression and deformation in the radial direction when subjected to operational forces. Notably, while the elastic portion (29) makes physical contact with the rigid portion (30), it is not bonded or affixed to it. This unbonded contact arrangement allows the elastic portion to move and deform more freely against the rigid portion, which can enhance the overall damping characteristics of the device by permitting a degree of relative movement between the two components without the constraints that a bonded connection would impose.

# Vibration Damping Device

## Technical Field

This invention relates to a vibration damping device, also known as a vibration isolator or anti-vibration mount, used in various applications such as automotive engine mounts, suspension bushings, and industrial machinery isolators. More specifically, it relates to a fluid-filled type vibration damping device that utilizes the flow of an incompressible liquid between chambers to achieve superior damping characteristics across a range of vibration frequencies.

## Background

Conventional fluid-filled vibration damping devices typically comprise a tubular outer attachment member and an inner attachment member, elastically connected to each other by a main rubber elastic body. A liquid chamber filled with a non-compressible liquid is formed within the device, and this chamber is often partitioned into two chambers—commonly referred to as a primary chamber and a secondary (or auxiliary) chamber—by a partition member. These chambers are connected via a restricted flow passage (orifice), through which the liquid flows back and forth in response to relative displacement between the outer and inner attachment members caused by input vibrations.

While this liquid flow through the restricted passage generates damping effects based on resonance phenomena, conventional designs face certain limitations. Specifically, the damping performance is often optimized for only a narrow frequency range, and achieving effective vibration damping across both low-frequency, large-amplitude vibrations (such as engine shake) and higher-frequency, small-amplitude vibrations (such as idling vibrations or booming noise) simultaneously has proven challenging using simple orifice-based designs alone. Additionally, many conventional structures rely on complex mechanical valves or moving plates to switch damping characteristics, which can increase manufacturing costs, reduce durability, and introduce reliability concerns over the operational life of the device.

## Summary of the Invention

In order to solve the problems described above, the present invention provides a novel vibration damping device with an improved partition structure that achieves superior damping performance through a simplified, durable configuration.

### Basic Structure

The vibration damping device according to this invention includes a tubular outer attachment member and a tubular inner attachment member, both preferably formed from a rigid material such as metal or hard resin. These two members are elastically connected to one another by a pair of main rubber elastic bodies that are spaced apart from each other in the axial direction of the device. This dual main rubber body configuration helps distribute the elastic support characteristics and contributes to the overall structural integrity of the mount while allowing for tuned spring characteristics in multiple directions.

Between the outer and inner attachment members, and bounded in part by the main rubber elastic bodies, a liquid chamber is formed and filled with a suitable non-compressible liquid, such as an ethylene glycol-based fluid or similar working fluid. This liquid chamber is divided into a first chamber and a second chamber by a partition portion disposed axially between the pair of main rubber elastic bodies.

### Partition Portion Configuration

The partition portion is a critical feature of this invention and comprises two primary components:

1. **An annular rigid portion** – This component is formed from a rigid material and includes a restricted passage (orifice) formed therein or along its periphery. This restricted passage provides fluid communication between the first chamber and the second chamber, allowing the working liquid to flow between the two chambers in response to relative displacement of the outer and inner attachment members during vibration input. The dimensions of this passage (length and cross-sectional area) can be tuned to target specific frequency ranges for effective damping via liquid resonance.

2. **An annular elastic portion** – Positioned adjacent to the annular rigid portion, this elastic portion is formed from a rubber-like elastic material. Unlike conventional designs where such elastic components might be bonded or vulcanized directly to the rigid portion, in this invention the annular elastic portion is arranged such that it is not bonded to the rigid portion at the region of contact.

### Key Structural Innovation

The distinguishing feature of this vibration damping device lies in the specific configuration and behavior of the annular elastic portion relative to the annular rigid portion. In this design, the annular elastic portion is configured such that, under the influence of internal liquid pressure or through structural pre-compression during assembly, it undergoes radial compression and deformation, bringing it into direct contact with the annular rigid portion in the axial or radial direction—yet critically, this contact occurs in an **unbonded state**.

This unbonded contact configuration represents a significant departure from conventional partition designs, where elastic and rigid components are typically fixed together through vulcanization bonding or mechanical fasteners. By allowing the elastic portion to contact the rigid portion without a fixed bond, the elastic portion retains a degree of freedom to deform and move relative to the rigid portion in response to varying pressure conditions within the liquid chambers.

### Mechanism and Advantages

This novel unbonded contact structure provides several important advantages:

**Pressure-Responsive Behavior**: Under low-frequency, large-amplitude vibration inputs, the pressure differential between the first and second chambers becomes substantial. This pressure differential compresses the elastic portion against the rigid portion, effectively increasing the rigidity of the partition structure at these frequencies. This increased rigidity helps promote effective liquid flow through the restricted passage, maximizing the liquid column resonance effect and enhancing damping performance for large-amplitude, low-frequency vibrations such as those experienced during engine shake conditions.

**Frequency-Selective Response**: Conversely, under high-frequency, small-amplitude vibration inputs—where the pressure differential between chambers is comparatively small—the elastic portion may separate slightly from the rigid portion or exhibit reduced compressive contact. This allows the elastic portion to behave in a more flexible, absorptive manner, effectively reducing dynamic spring constant at these higher frequencies and improving the isolation of small-amplitude vibrations, such as idling vibrations or booming noise, which are typically associated with higher frequency ranges.

**Simplified Construction**: By achieving this frequency-dependent, pressure-responsive behavior through the unbonded contact between the elastic and rigid portions—rather than through complex mechanical valve mechanisms, movable plates, or multiple orifice paths—the overall structure of the vibration damping device is considerably simplified. This simplification leads to reduced manufacturing complexity, lower production costs, and improved long-term durability, as there are fewer moving mechanical parts subject to wear or fatigue failure.

**Elimination of Bonding-Related Stress**: Furthermore, because the elastic portion is not bonded to the rigid portion at the point of contact, issues related to bonding failure, delamination, or stress concentration at the bond interface—which can occur in conventional bonded designs due to repeated cyclic loading—are effectively eliminated. This contributes to improved durability and consistent performance of the device throughout its service life.

### Additional Embodiments

In certain embodiments, the annular rigid portion and the annular elastic portion may be arranged concentrically, with the elastic portion positioned radially inward or outward relative to the rigid portion, such that radial compression of the elastic portion—caused by internal liquid pressure acting upon it—brings it into contact with an inner or outer surface of the rigid portion.

In other embodiments, the degree of compression and the resulting contact area between the elastic portion and rigid portion may be tuned by adjusting the initial gap distance, the thickness and material hardness of the elastic portion, and the shape of the rigid portion's contact surface. This allows the damping characteristics of the device to be finely tuned for specific vehicle or application requirements, providing designers with additional flexibility to optimize performance across the desired range of operating frequencies and vibration amplitudes.

### Conclusion

Through this innovative arrangement, wherein an annular elastic portion is designed to radially compress and deform into unbonded contact with an adjacent annular rigid portion containing a restricted flow passage, this vibration damping device achieves enhanced, frequency-dependent damping performance while maintaining a relatively simple, durable, and cost-effective construction. This structural configuration effectively addresses the limitations of conventional fluid-filled vibration damping devices, providing improved isolation and damping performance across both low-frequency, large-amplitude and high-frequency, small-amplitude vibration inputs.

# The Word "The"

"The" is the most commonly used word in the English language, yet it often goes unnoticed despite its constant presence in our speech and writing. As the definite article, it serves a crucial grammatical function: specifying particular nouns rather than general ones.

## Grammatical Function

When we say "the book" instead of "a book," we're indicating a specific book that both speaker and listener presumably know about. This distinguishes "the" from indefinite articles like "a" or "an," which refer to any unspecified member of a category. This small distinction carries significant meaning—compare "I saw a dog in the park" (any dog) versus "I saw the dog in the park" (a specific, previously mentioned or known dog).

## Historical Origins

"The" derives from Old English "þe," which itself evolved from earlier Germanic demonstrative pronouns related to "that" and "this." Its history reflects the broader evolution of English as it absorbed influences from Old Norse, Latin, and French while gradually simplifying its grammatical structures.

## Frequency and Ubiquity

Linguistic studies consistently show "the" as the most frequently occurring word in English texts, appearing far more often than any other word. This ubiquity makes it a cornerstone of natural language processing algorithms and a key indicator in linguistic analysis. Its ordinariness is precisely what makes it interesting—we rely on it so heavily that removing it from speech would make communication feel stilted and unnatural, as anyone who has tried to learn a language without articles (like Russian or Japanese) can attest when transitioning to English.

## Cultural and Symbolic Weight

Beyond grammar, "the" has taken on symbolic importance in titles and branding. Companies and creators often add "The" before a name to convey definitiveness or authority—"The New York Times," "The Rolling Stones," "The Ohio State University." This usage suggests exclusivity or preeminence, implying there is only one true version of what follows.

## Conclusion

Despite its small size and lack of independent meaning, "the" plays an outsized role in how we communicate. It shapes clarity, specificity, and even prestige in language, proving that even the most modest words can carry substantial weight in human communication.

# Patent Claim Summary
## Vibration Damping Device with Dual Rubber Elastic Bodies and Partitioned Liquid Chamber

### Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to a vibration damping device suitable for use in automotive engine mounts, suspension bushings, and industrial machinery isolators, and more particularly to a fluid-filled vibration damping device incorporating two main rubber elastic portions and a partitioned liquid-filled chamber structure.

---

### Claim Summary

**Claim 1 (Independent Claim):**

A vibration damping device comprising:

a) a first mounting member and a second mounting member disposed in spaced relation to one another for connection to a vibration-generating member and a vibration-receiving member, respectively;

b) a first main rubber elastic body interposed between and elastically connecting the first mounting member and an intermediate member, the first main rubber elastic body being configured to provide primary elastic support;

c) a second main rubber elastic body interposed between the intermediate member and the second mounting member, the second main rubber elastic body being configured to provide supplementary elastic support and cooperating with the first main rubber elastic body to define a sealed liquid chamber therebetween;

d) a partition member disposed within the liquid chamber, the partition member dividing the liquid chamber into a first sub-chamber and a second sub-chamber, wherein at least a portion of a wall of the first sub-chamber is defined by the first main rubber elastic body and at least a portion of a wall of the second sub-chamber is defined by the second main rubber elastic body;

e) each of the first sub-chamber and the second sub-chamber being filled with a non-compressible liquid; and

f) a restricted orifice passage formed in or adjacent the partition member, fluidly connecting the first sub-chamber and the second sub-chamber, the restricted orifice passage being dimensioned to generate a flow resistance and/or resonance effect in the liquid as it flows between the first sub-chamber and the second sub-chamber upon relative displacement of the first mounting member and the second mounting member, thereby producing a damping force.

---

**Claim 2 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, wherein the restricted orifice passage comprises a tuning passage having a cross-sectional area and length selected to produce a resonance-based damping effect at a predetermined target frequency range corresponding to low-frequency, large-amplitude vibration input.

**Claim 3 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, wherein the intermediate member comprises a rigid annular or block-shaped member disposed generally centrally between the first mounting member and the second mounting member, the first main rubber elastic body and the second main rubber elastic body being bonded to opposite axial sides of the intermediate member.

**Claim 4 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, wherein the partition member comprises a rigid or semi-rigid plate having a peripheral wall portion fixed relative to the intermediate member, and wherein the restricted orifice passage is formed as a groove extending circumferentially along an outer peripheral surface of the partition member, the groove being closed on an outer side by an inner circumferential surface of a surrounding sleeve member.

**Claim 5 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, wherein the first sub-chamber functions as a receiving chamber whose internal volume varies primarily in response to elastic deformation of the first main rubber elastic body, and wherein the second sub-chamber functions as an equilibrium chamber whose internal volume varies primarily in response to elastic deformation of the second main rubber elastic body.

**Claim 6 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, further comprising a flexible diaphragm forming at least a portion of a wall of the second sub-chamber, the flexible diaphragm being configured to accommodate volumetric changes in the non-compressible liquid without generating substantial elastic resistance.

**Claim 7 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, wherein the first main rubber elastic body and the second main rubber elastic body are formed with differing spring constants, such that the vibration damping device exhibits a first dynamic spring characteristic in a first frequency range and a second, different dynamic spring characteristic in a second frequency range.

**Claim 8 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, wherein the first mounting member includes a mounting bolt or stud extending along a central axis, and wherein the second mounting member comprises an outer cylindrical sleeve surrounding the first main rubber elastic body, the second main rubber elastic body, the intermediate member, and the partition member.

**Claim 9 (Dependent):**

The vibration damping device of claim 1, wherein the restricted orifice passage is further configured with a second orifice passage of differing cross-sectional area and/or length, the first and second orifice passages being selectively engageable to provide switchable damping characteristics corresponding to different vibration input frequency ranges.

**Claim 10 (Independent - Method Claim):**

A method of damping vibration transmitted between a vibration-generating member and a vibration-receiving member, the method comprising:

providing a vibration damping device according to claim 1 interposed between the vibration-generating member and the vibration-receiving member;

elastically deforming the first main rubber elastic body and the second main rubber elastic body in response to relative displacement between the first mounting member and the second mounting member; and

flowing the non-compressible liquid between the first sub-chamber and the second sub-chamber through the restricted orifice passage so as to generate a damping force opposing the relative displacement.

---

### Notes for Drafting Refinement

- Consider adding claims directed to specific orifice geometries (e.g., spiral, arcuate, multi-turn) for frequency tuning.
- Additional dependent claims may address manufacturing methods (e.g., vulcanization bonding of rubber to metal fittings).
- Claims could be expanded to cover a **movable member** (e.g., a rubber or resin plate) disposed within one sub-chamber to provide additional low-amplitude vibration isolation via microdisplacement, if applicable to the specific embodiment.
- Ensure consistency in antecedent basis for all claim terms across the full claim set prior to filing.

# Technical Abstract

**Vibration Isolator with Partitioned Elastic Chamber Structure**

This disclosure describes a fluid-filled vibration isolator apparatus configured to attenuate mechanical vibrations transmitted between two structural components, such as an engine and a vehicle chassis. The isolator comprises an outer attachment member and an inner attachment member arranged in a coaxial or spaced relationship, with the inner member positioned to receive a primary vibration source input.

A main rubber elastic body is interposed between the outer and inner attachment members, providing primary load-bearing elasticity and establishing a fluid-tight seal that partitions an interior chamber into at least a primary fluid chamber and an auxiliary fluid chamber. These chambers are filled with a non-compressible fluid and are configured to permit controlled fluid communication.

A distinguishing feature of the isolator is a partition member disposed within the fluid-filled interior, separating the primary and auxiliary chambers while permitting restricted fluid flow through a defined orifice passage. The partition member is characterized by a composite construction comprising an annular rigid portion, formed from a metal or high-modulus polymeric material, integrally bonded or mechanically joined to an annular elastic portion. This elastic portion is preferably formed of a rubber-like material and may function as a movable diaphragm or flexible membrane, capable of elastic deformation in response to internal fluid pressure fluctuations.

The composite rigid-elastic partition structure enables the isolator to exhibit frequency-dependent damping and dynamic stiffness characteristics, wherein low-frequency, large-amplitude vibrations induce fluid flow through the orifice passage (providing viscous damping), while high-frequency, small-amplitude vibrations are absorbed primarily through elastic deformation of the annular elastic portion of the partition member, effectively decoupling the fluid mass from the vibration input at higher frequencies. This dual-mode operation allows the isolator to achieve broadband vibration and noise attenuation while minimizing dynamic spring rate increases (anti-resonance stiffening) typically associated with conventional fluid-filled mounts at higher frequencies.

The resulting isolator construction offers improved vibration isolation performance across a wide frequency spectrum, enhanced durability due to reduced stress concentration through the rigid-elastic partition interface, and design flexibility for tuning damping and stiffness characteristics independently through selection of the elastic portion's geometry, thickness, and material properties.

# Fluid-Filled Vibration Damping Device

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to fluid-filled elastic mounting devices, and more particularly to a fluid-filled engine mount for supporting a power unit on a vehicle body in a vibration-damping manner, the mount being of the type having a partition structure that divides a fluid chamber into two liquid-filled chambers communicating with each other through a restricted orifice passage.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Fluid-filled elastic mounts are conventionally utilized in automotive and industrial applications for damping and isolating vibrations transmitted between two structural members, such as a power unit and a vehicle body. Such devices typically achieve vibration damping through the flow of an incompressible fluid between two liquid chambers via a restricted passage, whereby resonance of the fluid column produces a damping effect based on flow resistance and pressure differentials generated during relative displacement of the mount's elastic body.

However, conventional constructions have exhibited certain limitations with respect to durability, tuning flexibility across multiple vibration frequency ranges, and structural compactness. There exists a need in the art for an improved fluid-filled mount structure that overcomes these limitations while providing a robust, reliable damping performance over an extended service life.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

It is accordingly an object of the present invention to provide a fluid-filled engine mount having improved damping characteristics through a novel arrangement of a tubular outer member, an inner member, dual elastic rubber bodies, and a partition member.

According to one aspect of the present invention, there is provided a fluid-filled vibration damping device comprising:

a substantially tubular outer member;

an inner member disposed radially inwardly of the outer member in radially spaced-apart relation thereto;

a first elastic body interposed between and elastically connecting the inner member and an axial end portion of the outer member;

a second elastic body interposed between and elastically connecting the inner member and another axial end portion of the outer member, the first and second elastic bodies cooperating to define therebetween a fluid chamber filled with a non-compressible fluid;

a partition member disposed within the fluid chamber so as to divide the fluid chamber into a first liquid chamber and a second liquid chamber; and

a restricted passage formed so as to permit fluid communication between the first liquid chamber and the second liquid chamber, whereby relative displacement of the inner member and the outer member in a direction of principal vibration input induces flow of the fluid through the restricted passage between the first and second liquid chambers to exhibit a damping effect based on resonance and flow resistance of the fluid flowing therethrough.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENTS

### General Structure

Referring now to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals designate corresponding parts throughout the several views, there is shown in **FIG. 1** a fluid-filled engine mount **10** constructed according to a preferred embodiment of the present invention.

The engine mount **10** includes a tubular outer member **12** made of a rigid material such as metal or a fiber-reinforced hard plastic, and an inner member **14**, also formed of a rigid material, disposed radially inwardly of the outer member **12** so as to be spaced apart therefrom in a radial direction. The inner member **14** is adapted to be fixed to one of a power unit and a vehicle body, while the outer member **12** is adapted to be fixed to the other of the power unit and the vehicle body, such that vibrational loads generated during operation of the power unit are transmitted through the mount **10**.

### Elastic Bodies

A first rubber elastic body **16** is disposed so as to elastically connect the inner member **14** to a first axial end portion of the outer member **12**, while a second rubber elastic body **18** is disposed so as to elastically connect the inner member **14** to a second axial end portion of the outer member **12**, opposite the first axial end portion. The first rubber elastic body **16** and the second rubber elastic body **18** are preferably formed as generally frustoconical or annular bodies of vulcanized rubber, and are advantageously bonded to the respective outer circumferential surface of the inner member **14** and the respective inner circumferential surface of the outer member **12** by a vulcanization bonding process, whereby the first rubber elastic body **16** and second rubber elastic body **18** may be simultaneously formed and integrally bonded to the inner member **14** and outer member **12** in a unitary vulcanization step.

The first rubber elastic body **16** and the second rubber elastic body **18** cooperatively define, in an axial region therebetween, a fluid chamber **20** which is filled with a suitable non-compressible fluid, such as water, an alkylene glycol, a silicone oil, or a mixture thereof. It will be appreciated that the provision of dual elastic bodies **16**, **18** as described advantageously permits distribution of the load-bearing function between the two rubber elastic bodies, thereby enhancing durability and permitting a desired degree of freedom in tuning of spring characteristics for each of the axial directions and the radial directions of vibrational input.

### Partition Member

Disposed within the fluid chamber **20** is a partition member **22**, which extends generally in a radial direction so as to divide the fluid chamber **20** into a first liquid chamber **24** on a side thereof adjacent to the first rubber elastic body **16**, and a second liquid chamber **26** on a side thereof adjacent to the second rubber elastic body **18**. The partition member **22** is preferably formed of a rigid material such as metal or hard resin, and is fixed relative to at least one of the inner member **14** and the outer member **12** so as to occupy a substantially fixed position within the fluid chamber **20**.

The partition member **22** is formed, at a peripheral portion thereof, with a restricted passage **28** which places the first liquid chamber **24** and second liquid chamber **26** into mutual fluid communication. The restricted passage **28** preferably extends circumferentially about the partition member **22** in the form of a tunnel-shaped conduit of a predetermined cross-sectional area and length, such that a ratio of the cross-sectional area to the length of the restricted passage **28** is tuned in accordance with a target vibration frequency range sought to be damped.

### Operation

In operation, when a vibrational load is input between the inner member **14** and the outer member **12** in a direction generally corresponding to an axial direction of the mount **10**, the inner member **14** is caused to be displaced relative to the outer member **12**, whereby the volume of the first liquid chamber **24** and the volume of the second liquid chamber **26** are caused to vary in a complementary and generally inverse manner due to elastic deformation of the first rubber elastic body **16** and the second rubber elastic body **18**. Such variation in the respective chamber volumes induces a flow of the fluid between the first liquid chamber **24** and the second liquid chamber **26** through the restricted passage **28**.

By appropriately tuning the dimensions of the restricted passage **28**, in particular the cross-sectional area and length thereof, a resonance frequency of the fluid column flowing through the restricted passage **28** may be tuned to coincide with a target vibration frequency, such as an engine shake frequency or an idling vibration frequency, whereby a substantial damping effect based on the flow resistance and resonance behavior of the fluid is exhibited so as to effectively attenuate vibrations transmitted between the power unit and the vehicle body.

### Alternative Embodiments

While the foregoing describes a preferred embodiment wherein the partition member **22** is provided as a single, generally disk-shaped element, it is to be understood that the partition member **22** may alternatively be constructed of a plurality of separate members assembled together, or may incorporate a movable plate or diaphragm portion so as to accommodate minute pressure fluctuations within the fluid chamber, without departing from the scope of the present invention.

It is also to be understood that the first rubber elastic body **16** and the second rubber elastic body **18** may be provided with varying spring rates, wall thicknesses, and geometric profiles, so as to provide differing degrees of stiffness in the axial and radial directions, respectively, according to the particular application and vibration characteristics sought to be addressed.

## CLAIMS (Representative)

**1.** A fluid-filled vibration damping device, comprising:
a tubular outer member;
an inner member disposed radially inwardly of said outer member in a spaced-apart relationship;
a first elastic body elastically connecting said inner member to a first axial end of said outer member;
a second elastic body elastically connecting said inner member to a second axial end of said outer member, said first and second elastic bodies defining therebetween a fluid chamber filled with a non-compressible fluid;
a partition member disposed within said fluid chamber and dividing said fluid chamber into a first liquid chamber and a second liquid chamber; and
a restricted passage formed in said partition member and providing fluid communication between said first liquid chamber and said second liquid chamber.

**2.** The fluid-filled vibration damping device according to claim 1, wherein said first elastic body and said second elastic body are each formed of vulcanized rubber bonded to said inner member and said outer member.

counterfactuals.output:
# Annular Elastic Portion Compression in Vibration Damper Partitions

## Structural Configuration

In vibration damper assemblies, the partition member typically comprises a **rigid portion** (often formed of metal or hard resin) and an **elastic portion** (formed of rubber or elastomeric material) that are configured in an annular relationship. The formal patent terminology for this arrangement generally describes the elastic portion as being **"interposed"** between structural elements or **"disposed radially inward/outward"** relative to the rigid portion.

## Mechanism of Radial Compression

The compression mechanism can be characterized through the following patent-style language:

**1. Press-Fit or Interference Fit Configuration**
The annular elastic portion is described as having an **outer diametrical dimension** (or inner diametrical dimension, depending on configuration) that is **"set to be larger than"** the corresponding dimension of the mating rigid portion **"in a free state"** (i.e., prior to assembly). This creates an **interference relationship**.

**2. Assembly-Induced Deformation**
Upon assembly, the elastic portion is **"elastically deformed"** or **"compressed in a radial direction"** as it is press-fitted, inserted, or otherwise assembled with the rigid portion. This is often stated as:

> "the annular elastic portion is compressed radially inward (or outward) by the rigid portion so as to be held in **close contact** therewith"

**3. Non-Bonded Contact Relationship**
Critically, the patent language specifies that this contact is achieved **"without being bonded"** or is characterized as a **"non-adhesive contact state."** Common phrasings include:

> "the elastic portion is held in contact with the rigid portion **by an elastic restoring force** thereof, without being fixed thereto by an adhesive or vulcanization bonding"

or

> "the elastic portion and the rigid portion are configured to be held in **mutual contact by a compressive force** generated by elastic deformation, thereby forming a **liquid-tight seal** or **sealing contact** independent of adhesive bonding"

## Functional Basis for Non-Bonded Retention

The retention without bonding is justified in patent claims by reference to the **restoring force (repulsive force)** inherent in the elastic material:

> "the elastic portion, being compressed radially between the rigid portion and [another structural member], generates a **reaction force** sufficient to maintain sealing contact and positional retention **without requiring an adhesive layer or vulcanized bond**"

This is sometimes further supported by describing surface texturing or a **"fitting groove"** and **"fitting protrusion"** relationship, wherein the compressed elastic portion mechanically engages a groove or step in the rigid portion, providing retention through geometric interference and elastic clamping force alone, rather than through chemical or adhesive bonding.

## Summary of Key Claim Elements

A representative claim limitation might read:

> "wherein the annular elastic portion is configured to be **radially compressed** between the rigid portion and [adjacent member] so as to be held in **liquid-tight contact** therewith **by an elastic force** of the elastic portion, **independent of any bonding** between the elastic portion and the rigid portion."

This terminology emphasizes (1) the **pre-assembly dimensional interference**, (2) the **elastic deformation upon assembly**, and (3) the **retention mechanism based purely on mechanical/elastic force**, expressly excluding adhesive or vulcanization bonding as the retention means.

# Patent Claim: Liquid-Filled Vibration Damping Mount

## Claim 1

A liquid-filled vibration damping device comprising:

an inner attachment member adapted to be connected to one of a vibration generating member and a vibration receiving member;

an outer attachment member disposed radially outward of and spaced apart from said inner attachment member, said outer attachment member adapted to be connected to the other of the vibration generating member and the vibration receiving member;

a main rubber elastic body interposed between and elastically connecting said inner attachment member and said outer attachment member, said main rubber elastic body providing fluid-tight sealing across a first axial end of said outer attachment member;

a flexible diaphragm disposed so as to close off a second axial end of said outer attachment member opposite said main rubber elastic body, said flexible diaphragm being elastically deformable;

a fluid chamber defined between said main rubber elastic body and said flexible diaphragm, said fluid chamber containing a non-compressible fluid sealed therein;

a partition member disposed within said fluid chamber so as to divide said fluid chamber into a first fluid chamber partially defined by said main rubber elastic body and a second fluid chamber partially defined by said flexible diaphragm, said partition member comprising:

  (a) a rigid annular member having a substantially annular shape and formed of a rigid material, said rigid annular member being fixed relative to said outer attachment member; and

  (b) an elastic annular member formed of a rubber-like elastic material, said elastic annular member being disposed radially inward of said rigid annular member and integrally connected thereto, said elastic annular member cooperating with said rigid annular member to define therebetween a restricted flow passage extending circumferentially so as to fluidly communicate said first fluid chamber and said second fluid chamber;

wherein said restricted flow passage is dimensioned to permit resonant flow of said non-compressible fluid between said first fluid chamber and said second fluid chamber upon relative displacement between said inner attachment member and said outer attachment member, thereby exhibiting a vibration damping effect based on fluid flow action through said restricted flow passage.

---

## Claim 2 (Dependent)

The liquid-filled vibration damping device according to claim 1, wherein said rigid annular member includes an outer peripheral cylindrical portion fixed to an inner circumferential surface of said outer attachment member, and an inwardly extending flange portion extending radially inward from said outer peripheral cylindrical portion, said restricted flow passage being formed as a groove open toward one axial side of said inwardly extending flange portion and closed off on the other axial side by an adjacent wall surface.

---

## Claim 3 (Dependent)

The liquid-filled vibration damping device according to claim 2, wherein said elastic annular member is vulcanization-bonded to an inner circumferential edge of said inwardly extending flange portion of said rigid annular member, and includes a central through-hole permitting axial fluid communication in cooperation with at least one aperture formed through said partition member, said central through-hole and said aperture defining, in combination with said restricted flow passage, a tuned fluid flow path having a predetermined resonance frequency corresponding to a targeted vibration frequency range.

---

## Claim 4 (Dependent)

The liquid-filled vibration damping device according to claim 1, wherein said elastic annular member further functions as a movable rubber plate portion capable of elastic deformation in response to minute relative displacement between said first fluid chamber and said second fluid chamber, thereby absorbing pressure fluctuations of a frequency higher than a resonance frequency of said restricted flow passage.

---

## Claim 5 (Dependent)

The liquid-filled vibration damping device according to claim 1, wherein said restricted flow passage extends substantially over an entire circumference of said partition member and is dimensioned in cross-sectional area and circumferential length so as to exhibit a resonance frequency corresponding to a low-frequency, large-amplitude vibration input, whereby said non-compressible fluid flowing through said restricted flow passage between said first fluid chamber and said second fluid chamber generates a damping force effective to attenuate said low-frequency, large-amplitude vibration.
